Final Judgment : Acquittal  JUDGMENT Brief Statement of reasons for the decision of the case:
1.

The prosecution seeks to prove against the accused persons that on or before 15.09.2004, all the accused persons being the Directors / Managers / Employees /
Authorized Signatories of the company M/s Map Chit Fund Pvt. Ltd., entered into criminal conspiracy to induce complainant Sh. B.K. Gupta and several other persons to become the member of chit fund schemes floated by M/s Map Chit Fund Pvt. Ltd.
on assurance to get good returns on the invested amount and in this way collected a huge amount from public at large including of complainant and after collecting several lakhs i.e. Rs.65 lacs approximately from the investors, vanished with the money of the investors, after locking and closing of the offices of the company at Sector-7, Rohini, Delhi and in this process, cheated several persons including the complainant Sh. B.K. Gupta and other investors.
FIR No.812/2004 P.S- Saraswati Vihar State Vs. Parveen Jain Etc.
2.

The accused persons were formally charged for the offence U/s 420/120B IPC on 13.05.2013 to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
3. On perusal of file shows that the Bank Official was filed the compliance report of order dated 11.10.2023.

As per the compliance report, the settlement amount has been released to the 18 co-complainants as per the settlement arrived between the co-complainants and the accused persons vide settlement dated 12.01.2018.
The Inspector Dheeraj Kumar also confirmed the same.
The copies of the drafts released to the co-complainants and their receivings have also been filed on record.

In view of the same, the settlement agreement dated 12.01.2018 has been completed and the offences under Section 420/120B IPC with the permission of the Court stands compounded against the accused persons qua the 17 co- complainants as mentioned in the mediation order dated 12.01.2018 and one another complainant Sh. Sushil Kumar.

The matter was at the stage of PE.

Witnesses, namely, Bhagwati Prasad, Balbir Kaur, Ram Chandra, Anguri Devi, Shiv Kumar, Anil Rana and Smt. Lakshmi were hereby dropped vide order dated 29.04.2023 as they were remained unserved through DCP concerned.
Witnesses, namely, Yash Pal Khatri, Seema Manocha and B.D. Sharma, were already dropped due to death through DCP FIR No.812/2004 P.S- Saraswati Vihar State Vs. Parveen Jain Etc. concerned.
Witnesses Satya Prakash Dabas and Vivek Sharma have not supported the prosecution case.
No other public witness remains to be examined.
Other witnesses are formal in nature.
No purpose will be served by examining other formal witnesses.
4. Till date, the prosecution has examined six witnesses.

5. Ms. Sheela Vats, (PW1) deposed that in 2006, she along with her family were residing at B-56,
2nd Floor, Hari Nagar, Delhi.
Accused Shyam Lal Kaushik is brother-in-law of her daughter Poonam Bhardwaj.
Accused Shyam Lal Kaushik was running one Chit Fund namely M/s Map Chits Pvt. Ltd.
She correctly identified the accused Shyam Lal Kaushik present in the Court.
In total, she invested amount of Rs.1 lac, her daughter invested Rs.1 lac and Shashi Vashisht invested Rs.50,000/-.
The office of M/s Map Chits Pvt. Ltd. situated in Rohini and Kohat Enclave.
She started investing the money in the said chit fund from 01.05.2002 till November 2002.
Her daughter started investing money from 01.05.2022 till January 2004.
Accused Manorama Kaushik was the Director of Map Chit Fund.
She correctly identified the accused Manorama Kaushik present in the Court.
Accused Praveen Jain was also the partner of the Map Chit Fund.
She correctly identified the accused Praveen Jain present in the Court.
She correctly identified the accused Anita Garg and Harikishan Garg present in the Court and they were working with the accused Manorama Kaushik.

One person,

She invested the money in two scheme and in one of them, she invested the money for two days.
PW1 was cross-examined at length and discharged.

EOW and on that day, further investigation of present case was marked to him.
He received report of CA (Chartered Accountant) and of GEQD report.

8. Sh. Dharam Dutt Sharma (PW3) deposed that in the year 2002, accused persons, namely, S.K.
Kaushik and H.K. Garg came to meet him and told that they had started a Chit - Fund Company in the name of Manorama Kaushik and Anita Garg.
The name of the said Chit - Fund Company was Map Chit Fund Company.
He does not remember the tenure of investment which was assured by accused persons but assured him that they shall give him a good return.
On the basis of their assurance, he opened two accounts in the name of his son Narender and himself.
Time to time, he kepts investing in the said company and they also used him the receipt against his investment.
The receipt is Ex.PW3/A (OSR).
The said receipt was given to him by accused Surender.
After some months, one of his known persons informed him that said Map company had closed its office and they had run away with the money of public at large.
He went to their office at Kohat Enclave and found that there was lock on their office.
Accused persons, namely, Shalender Kaushik and his wife Manorama Kaushik are his distant relatives.
Cross-examination is Nil.
Opportunity given.
9. Sh. Vikrant Gupta, (PW4) deposed that in the year 2001 his father took VRS from the State Bank of India.
At that time, his father was having some money to invest.
Therefore, his father opened two accounts in MAP Chit-Fund Company.
One account was in the name of his father and another was in his name.
He stated that he does not remember the total amount FIR No.812/2004 P.S- Saraswati Vihar State Vs. Parveen Jain Etc. invested by them but it is correct that they had paid their total amount.
After some time, when they asked accused persons to return their money, they kept pending it on one pretext or another.
After some time, they came to know that the said company had closed its office and all its Directors had run away with the money of public.
They had not received even a single penny.
He stated that he is not having the receipts issued by the accused persons.
As far as, he could remember they had paid about Rs.3,00,000/- i.e. Rs.1,50,000/- for each account.
Accused persons, namely, S.L. Kaushik, H.K. Garg and V.K. Mangal were known to him.
Cross-examination is Nil.
Opportunity given.
10. Sh. Kishan Pal, (PW5) deposed that in the year 2002 accused Surender came in his contact through one of his friends.
Accused Surender assured him that Map Chit Fund Company was a good option to invest and they were giving return at a good interest rate.

On the basis of said assurance,
he opened account in the said company.
He paid total 22 installments each was Rs.2,000/-.
In the year 2004, on his account being matured, he went to the office of said company to get his return and they told him that in the end of March 2004 they shall issue him a cheque.

In March 2004 when he State vs Parveen Jain Etc on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61043539/
4 did not receive his cheque, he again went to the said office in Kohat Enclave and found that said office was locked.
On enquiry, he came to know that Directors of said company had run away with the public money.
He has not received even a single penny from the said company.

Ltd. and he had received his amount which he invested in the abovesaid company.

12. Witnesses, namely, Bhagwati Prasad, Balbir Kaur, Ram Chandra, Anguri Devi, Shiv Kumar, Anil Rana and Smt. Lakshmi were hereby dropped vide order dated 29.04.2023 as they were remained unserved through DCP concerned.
Witnesses, namely, Yash Pal Khatri, Seema Manocha and B.D. Sharma, were already dropped due to death through DCP concerned.
Witnesses Satya Prakash Dabas and Vivek Sharma have not supported the prosecution case.
No other public witness remains to be examined.
Other witnesses are formal in nature.
No purpose will be served by examining other formal witnesses.
Accordingly, PE was closed and S.A. was dispensed with.
FIR No.812/2004 P.S- Saraswati Vihar State Vs. Parveen Jain Etc.

sentences.text: 13. Arguments were heard.
File perused.
14. To prove the allegations of offence, the complainant and the eye witness are the pivotal witnesses.
The witnesses, namely, PW1, PW3, PW4 and PW5 arrived at settlement with the accused persons and payment has been received as per the settlement.

Further, the witness PW2A and PW6 did not support the case of the prosecution and the other public witnesses did not step into the witness box for their examination to bring home the allegations against the accused persons for conviction.
The case of the prosecution rests on the testimony of the public witnesses.
However, as the remaining public witnesses were not examined, the allegations of cheating could not be substantiated against the accused persons.
The other witnesses are formal witnesses and only part of the investigation.
Their testimony in any case would have only proved the chain of investigation carried out and not the offence against the complainants.

In absence of any substantial and corroborative proof against the accused persons,
namely, (i) Smt. Manorama Kaushik W/o Sh. Shyam Lal Kaushik, (ii) Vinod Kumar Mangal S/o Sh.
Chiranji Lal, (iii) Har Kishan Garg S/o Sh. Ghamandi Lal Garg, (iv) Shyam Lal Kaushik S/o Sh.
Banwari Lal Kaushik, (v) Praveen Jain S/o Sh. Ghamandi Lal FIR No.812/2004 P.S- Saraswati Vihar State Vs. Parveen Jain Etc. Jain, (vi) Surender Kumar S/o late Sh. Mohar Singh and (vii) M/s Map Chits Pvt. Ltd., they are hereby stand acquitted for the offence under Section 420/120B IPC.
